title: G7, EU and Australia price cap on Russian seaborne crude oil takes effect
body:
A price cap of 60 US dollars per barrel on maritime Russian crude oil exports took effect on 5 December 2022. It was applied by the European Union, the G7 countries and Australia. Under the measure, G7 and EU tankers, insurers and credit institutions may handle Russian oil shipments to third countries only if the cargo is bought at or below the cap. The aim was to limit Russian revenue while keeping Russian oil flowing to global markets.

A similar measure on Russian petroleum products was expected to take effect on 5 February 2023, and the products cap level was not given at the time of the first announcement. The EU and G7 planned to review the level of the crude cap every two months, with the first review scheduled for mid-January 2023.

Japan, a G7 member, applied the 60 dollar cap but excluded crude from the Sakhalin-2 project, citing energy security. Russia said it would not abide by the measure, even if it had to cut oil production, and that it was preparing retaliatory measures. Later reporting by Al Jazeera noted that the crude cap stayed at 60 dollars for more than three years and that weak enforcement and a shadow fleet of tankers reduced its effect.
